Challenge in this writ petition is to the order dated 31.5.2022 passed by respondent 2 Assistant Collector/Tehsildar (First Class) District Ghaziabad in Case No. 6592 of 2021 Computerized Case No. T202111280106592 (Land Management Committee Vs.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for petitioner submits that petitioner was in rightful ownership and possession over the land in dispute.
Subsequently the land of the petitionere along with lands of other tenure holders were acquired under the National High Way Authority Act.
Consequently, a supplementary award dated 14.5.2019 was passed by the Additional District Magistrate/Land Acquisition Authority (Competent Authority).
The same is on record at page 25 of the paper book.

Petitioner was,
accordingly, awarded compensation, which was accepted by the petitioner.
On the above premise, the learned counsel for petitioner submits that proceedings under Section 67 of the U.P. Revenue Code 2006 are wholly illegal and without jurisdiction.
As such, the order impugned in present writ petition is liable to be quashed by this Court.
Learned Standing counsel has, however, opposed the present writ petition.
He submits that order impugned in present writ petition is appealable in terms of Section 67 (5) of the U.P. Revenue Code, 2006.
As such, petitioner has adequate and efficacious alternative remedy by way of an appeal against the order impugned.

He,
therefore, contends that present writ petition is liable to be dismissed on the ground of alternative remedy.
As such, However, he could not dislodge the factual/legal submissions urged by the learned counsel for petitioner with reference to the record at this stage.
Having heard the learned counsel for petitioner, the learned Standing Counsel representing respondents 1 and 2 and upon perusal of record, matter requires consideration.
Notice on behalf of opposite parties 1 and 2 has been accepted by the learned Standing Counsel.
He prays for and is granted six weeks time to file counter affidavit.
Petitioner will have one week thereafter to file rejoinder affidavit.

Considering the facts and circumstance of the case a noted herein above, as an interim measure, it is provided that until further orders of this Court, the effect and operation of the impugned order dated 31.5.2023 passed by respondent 2 Assistant Collector/Tehsildar (First Class) District Ghaziabad in Case No. 6592 of 2021 Computerized Case No. T202111280106592 (Land Management Committee Vs.
Farkan) (Annexure 1 to the writ petition) and consequential recovery pursuant to aforesaid order shall remain stayed."

From perusal of the interim order granted by writ Court, it is clear that only the order passed in proceedings under Section 67 of U.P. Revenue Code for eviction as well as the order imposing damages to the tune of Rs.11,62,800/- was stayed by writ Court.

Learned counsel for the applicant states that after passing of interim order dated 09.01.2024,
Additional District Magistrate (Land Revenue) had passed an order on 18.03.2024 requiring the applicant to return back the compensation amount of Rs.26,95,710/- paid to the applicant towards compensation of land which has been acquired.

This Court finds that no case for contempt is made out as the notice dated 18.03.2024 is an independent proceeding as the authorities have found that pursuant to arbitration the amount has wrongly been paid to the applicant amounting to Rs.26,95,710/- being the compensation for the land which has been acquired.

The interim order dated 09.01.2024 has no effect upon the notice issued by the authorities as writ Court had only stayed the eviction order in proceedings under Section 67 of U.P. Revenue Code and damages imposed by Sub Divisional Officer once the eviction order was passed.
In view of above, no case for contempt is made out.
The contempt application is misconceived and stands dismissed.
